The two previously-open facets both now have real evidence added to the same `tb_ppg_control_top_lifecycle_fault_adc_anomaly.v`: **Facet1** (branch ID) -- inside LFA-02a, the held-result discard record's color_ir/frame_type/sample_index are compared field-by-field against a real snapshot taken at the moment that exact transaction was set up, not just checked for any nonzero value. **Facet2** (transfer priority) -- a new `p01_facet2_ready_vs_abort_race` scenario genuinely races AMI's internal `flag_result_abort_discard` against `i_measurement_result_ready` on the same cycle and confirms discard wins deterministically (o_measurement_result_valid reads 0, discard fires with correct reason/identity, `cnt_result_capture` -- the file's own naive valid&&ready success counter -- does not advance), proving no double-recording. Two real construction bugs were found and fixed along the way, both in this new TB code, not the RTL: (1) the identity snapshot was originally captured after a wait loop, letting a real subsequent owner-commit overwrite it before use -- fixed by capturing immediately before `drive_real_adc_done`; (2) `i_control_abort_event` reaches AMI only after one cycle of registration through `ppg_control_top.v`'s own `flag_owner_abort_event` merge, while `i_measurement_result_ready` is a direct wire -- the first same-negedge construction actually let ready win by a full cycle before abort's registered effect ever reached AMI, never producing a genuine collision; fixed by pre-staging the abort pulse one cycle ahead so the registered signal is already live when ready arrives. A third, non-RTL timing trap was also worked around: STOP/abort drives lifecycle into STOPPING on its own, and if `i_adc_physical_idle` is allowed back high at that point, the scheduler's near-instant next-owner grant gets orphaned (Q1/Q2/Q3 generation appears to freeze once STOPPING begins) -- avoided by holding physical idle low through the race window, not by changing any RTL. Re-ran the whole file under iverilog: `LIFECYCLE_FAULT_ADC_ANOMALY_TB_PASS`, 0 FAIL, 79 PASS (including all 53 JNT-01~09 prerequisite checks). records.current_cell: **Cluster ⑥ finding, dangling output (whole-bus, likely oversight vs. intentional)**: `ppg_adc_result_router.v` has zero `always` blocks (pure combinational route-select, confirmed via full-file read: every output is a plain `assign o_X = i_X`, no registration). At AMI's instantiation (`ppg_adc_measurement_idac_integration.v:1938-1956`), **all 18 of router's shared-payload output ports are left empty** (`.o_calibrated_s1_value()` through `.o_dc_code_epoch()`), while its 3 branch-select valids (`o_amb_cal_valid`/`o_dc_cal_valid`/`o_normal_valid`) and `o_run_generation` ARE connected. This is not a functional bug: every downstream consumer (the NORMAL fork, and cross-cluster the IDAC controller for AMB/DCS) is wired directly to the **pre-router** wire (`dec_router_calibrated_s1_value` etc., the same wire that feeds router's own `i_calibrated_s1_value` input) rather than router's dangling output, which is bit-identical since router performs zero transformation on these fields -- confirmed at `ppg_normal_transaction_fork`'s own instantiation (`:1985`, `.i_calibrated_s1_value(dec_router_calibrated_s1_value)`, the identical wire router itself consumes). Router's own output ports for these 18 fields are therefore real, but functionally inert -- an intentional "skip the pass-through buffer" wiring optimization once verified, but recorded as a finding since it was not obviously reasoned from the port table alone. **Permanently dangling at the glue-top/DBG_OUT/P2S layer too, confirmed 2026-09-05 (P2 disposition pass)**: none of these 18 fields ever reach AMI's own top-level port list (C10) or `ppg_control_top.v`'s boundary -- they die at this AMI-internal instantiation, several hierarchy levels below Top -- so `PPG_CHIP_DIGITAL_TOP_SPI_P2S_INTEGRATION_CONTRACT.md` V1.5 §9 item 5's freeze on further `ppg_control_top.v` port/logic changes independently forecloses ever exposing them through the glue top, on top of the existing bypass already making them functionally moot. Same external-valid-gating mitigation applies. **Additional finding, dangling outputs (likely oversight)**: 11 of dc_recovery's 41 outputs are left empty at AMI's instantiation (`ppg_adc_measurement_idac_integration.v:2268-2290`) -- `o_programmable_15_calibration_applied`, `o_programmable_saturation_low/high` (3), and `o_detect_code`/`o_stage1_raw`/`o_stage1_code_ext`/`o_stage2_raw`/`o_stage2_code_ext`/`o_nominal_15_code`/`o_nominal_15_valid`/`o_nominal_saturated` (8) -- these are the raw diagnostic-passthrough fields that stop being forwarded once the module produces its own final coarse/fine PPG values; unlike router's whole-bus finding, these have no bypass wire either (the pre-dc_recovery values are consumed by the reconstructor->dc_recovery hop already, not duplicated onward) -- genuinely unreachable past this point, distinct from router's case. **Permanently dangling, confirmed 2026-09-05 (P2 disposition pass)**: none of these 11 fields reach AMI's own top-level port list (C10) or `ppg_control_top.v`'s boundary either, so `PPG_CHIP_DIGITAL_TOP_SPI_P2S_INTEGRATION_CONTRACT.md` V1.5 §9 item 5's freeze on further `ppg_control_top.v` port/logic change independently forecloses ever exposing them through the glue-top DBG_OUT/P2S path, on top of the RTL-level unreachability already noted. Not a TBD pending DBG_OUT design; not fixed (RTL unchanged).

records.current_cell: IDAC -> AMI private record -> C24 -> C01/C03/C02; no direct bypass. **Cluster ③ real-evidence upgrade**: the three lane sources are `CTX_AMB_FAULT_BIT`/`CTX_DCS_R_FAULT_BIT`/`CTX_DCS_IR_FAULT_BIT` (`ppg_idac_code_controller.v:170-172`), ORed into `o_controller_fault_blocking` (`:638`) and forwarded to AMI's `flag_idac_fault_active` (cause `8'h05` lane, `ppg_adc_measurement_idac_integration.v:2416`). **Real, already-fixed V2.3 deadlock** (documented at the RTL's own header, `ppg_idac_code_controller.v:26`, and in project memory [[feedback-idac-fault-bit-stop-not-start-clears]]): these three fault bits were previously cleared only in the `i_start_ack_event` block, but the contract (§11.3, lines 296-297 and 546) requires them to clear only via STOP/abort + idle + root-cause-gone (or async reset) -- a fresh START must never clear a pre-existing fault. The old (backwards) implementation meant a real AMB/DC_R/DC_IR search-exhaustion fault could never be cleared: `o_controller_fault_blocking` feeds AMI's `o_ami_fault_active` -> supervisor's `o_system_fault_blocking` -> manager's `flag_start_ready` gate, so no `i_start_ack_event` could ever fire to clear the very bits gated on that same event -- a genuine deadlock, confirmed by a real xsim run (Group 8's `tb_ppg_control_top_periodic_recheck_recovery.v`) that stuck at `o_start_ready=0`/`o_system_fault_blocking=1` indefinitely even after a full STOP+drain+`i_diag_clear_event` sequence. Fixed in V2.3 by moving the three clears into the `flag_control_cancel` block (STOP/abort/leave-RUN, `:580`, which already atomically clears pending context and forces `state_next=ST_IDLE`) and removing the old START-block clear entirely (the legitimate case of an illegal START *newly setting* these bits is untouched). Re-verified: Group 8's RRC-01~12 all pass under real xsim; a byte-for-byte iverilog A/B diff of the unit-level TB before/after showed zero behavior change.
